 Bharad Thirumalai Sat 21 November 2026 9:00, UK Don’t miss our Tottenham coverage Add SpursWeb as a Google Preferred Source to see more of our Tottenham news. Add to Preferred Sources Micky Hazard believes there is only one thing that could stop Tottenham star Luca Williams-Barnett from turning into the next Glenn Hoddle. 
 There is a huge amount of excitement at Hotspur Way surrounding Williams-Barnett , with the hype around the youngster being greater than any 18-year-old Spurs academy player, possibly going back decades.
 Tottenham have already sent a big hint that the teenager is now considered a full first-team player , which is evidenced by the fact that he has only featured once for the U21S all campaign.
 That is understandable as Williams-Barnett has looked a cut above the rest whenever he has played in Premier League 2, even though he has often come up against players who are three or four years older than him.
 What has added to the excitement about the teenager is that he looked the part in his two cameos off the bench in the Premier League over recent weeks.
 In fact, Williams-Barnett even won the Premier League Creative Moment of the Month award for October for his incredible piece of skill in his debut against Crystal Palace, which should have got him an assist.
 Credit: oscar.visualss / Instagram Micky Hazard reveals his warning to ‘incredibly special’ Tottenham starlet Luca Williams-Barnett
 According to recent reports, Tottenham have decided against loaning out the 18-year-old in January and expect him to get plenty of minutes for De Zerbi’s side over the coming weeks and months.
 MORE SPURS STORIES That goes against Spurs’ modus operandi of giving senior minutes in the EFL to their best young talent, which is perhaps further evidence that Williams-Barnett is seen as a cut above the rest, including the likes of Mikey Moore .
 Tottenham legend Micky Hazard believes that the 18-year-old has the ability to emulate the great Glenn Hoddle, given the fearlessness and creativity with which he plays.
 The former Spurs midfielder revealed that he met with Williams-Barnett at the training ground earlier this season, and shared that he advised the youngster not to have his natural flair coached out of him.
 Hazard told PA Sport : “I am a great believer in producing your own. What the homegrown do is they give the club its heart and soul because they know the importance of the club because they’ve come through the system.
 “When we talk about that we haven’t produced a real superstar since Harry Kane, I have to be honest with you and say we have one in the making now. I think Luca’s going to be something incredibly special. And the sooner we get him in that team, we can give him a chance to grow and develop because he’s got the lot from what I’ve seen of him.
 “I spoke to him at the dinner, I sat next to him and I said to him, ‘look Luca, please, all I ask of you, you’re such a special talent and don’t let English football change you’, because I said, ‘add to your game, add some of the things that they want you to add, but don’t let them change you’.
 “I said, ‘don’t let them take away that flair, that genius and that creativity because that’s you and that’s who you are and that’s who you are going to be. You’re going to be in the Glenn Hoddle mould, the fans are going to idolise and worship you, but if you change and become this up and down, run around and tackle, and lose that natural instinct you have, it will only be you to blame’.
 “Glenn went through the same process where managers tried to add this and that or take away this and that, but he was strong enough mentally to stick to his game and look at the worship he has experienced. Luca could be the next… different to Glenn Hoddle, but that mould because he is very special.”
 Spurs’ injury situation could give Williams-Barnett the platform he needs
 It has been reported since the start of the season that the Tottenham academy man has been making an excellent impression during first-team training.
 In fact, a club insider revealed that some at Spurs expect Williams-Barnett to be starting matches before the end of the season , with the youngster leaving his teammates ‘blown away’ in training.
 However, it appears that the youngster’s opportunities to secure a starting berth could come much sooner than many had anticipated.
 Mathys Tel’s injury could pave the way for Williams-Barnett to get starts in the Premier League after his impressive displays off the bench.
 With the Frenchman expected to be out for a few weeks, and with Wilson Odobert and Mykhailo Mudryk also on the treatment table, the 18-year-old could get a golden chance to make the left-wing spot his own.
